props.subTitle: Hidden Network
props.title: What Does the Lymphatic System Actually Do?
props.text: The lymphatic system is a network of vessels and lymph nodes that helps move excess fluid, transport immune cells, and remove everyday waste from body tissues. Unlike the circulatory system, it relies on breathing, movement, and muscle activity to keep lymph flowing. When this flow slows, fluid may build up, causing heaviness, puffiness, or mild swelling. Lymphatic Massage uses slow, rhythmic techniques to encourage natural lymph flow and help the body feel lighter and more balanced.
props.feature1Text: Encourages healthy lymph movement using light, rhythmic strokes.
props.feature2Text: Supports circulation, fluid movement, and everyday comfort.

items.question: Is Lymphatic Massage the same as Deep Tissue Massage?
items.answer: No. Deep Tissue Massage works on deeper muscle layers using firm pressure, while Lymphatic Massage uses very light, rhythmic movements that follow the body's lymphatic pathways to encourage natural fluid movement.

items.question: Can Lymphatic Massage help with swollen legs after travelling?
items.answer: Yes. Long flights, road trips, or extended periods of sitting may contribute to temporary fluid retention. Gentle lymphatic drainage is commonly chosen to help the legs feel lighter and more comfortable afterward.

items.question: Does Lymphatic Massage remove toxins from the body?
items.answer: The lymphatic system naturally helps transport waste products and excess fluid. Lymphatic Massage supports this normal function by encouraging healthy lymph movement, but it should not be considered a medical detox treatment.

items.question: Will the massage feel gentle?
items.answer: Yes. The pressure is intentionally light because lymph vessels sit close to the surface of the skin. Strong pressure is not necessary to encourage healthy lymph flow.

items.question: Can I combine Lymphatic Massage with other spa treatments?
items.answer: Absolutely. Many guests combine it with facials, reflexology, or relaxing body treatments to create a more complete wellness experience.

items.question: Is lymphatic drainage real?
items.answer: Yes. Lymphatic drainage is a gentle massage technique designed to encourage the movement of lymph fluid through the body. It is commonly used to help manage swelling and support relaxation.

items.question: Does lymphatic drainage work on the face?
items.answer: Yes. Facial lymphatic drainage uses gentle movements around the face and neck to encourage lymph flow. It may help reduce temporary puffiness and leave the face feeling refreshed.

items.question: Can lymphatic drainage make you sick?
items.answer: Lymphatic drainage is generally gentle, but some people may feel tired, thirsty, or slightly light-headed afterward. Drinking water and resting after the treatment can help. If you feel unwell or have a medical condition, consult a healthcare professional before having lymphatic drainage.
